title: fix(plugin-audit): forward the caller's execution envelope to the sys_comment sharing gates (#7141)
body:
Closes #7141.

`callerContext()` (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts`)
rebuilt a **five-field projection** of the caller's `ExecutionContext` before
handing it to `ISharingService.canEdit`, whose contract declares the **full**
envelope and whose doc block states callers "MUST NOT rebuild a subset of it"
(#6523 / the #6206 ruling). #7136 (PR #7140) widened the return *annotation* and
deliberately left the body; this is that deferred runtime change.

## Anchors re-verified at the branch point (`origin/main` @ `3415a61`)

| Claim | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| five-field projection | `comment-access-hooks.ts:202` | confirmed |
| `hasWriteBypass` fails closed by reading `context?.onBehalfOf?.userId` | `plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:704-707` | confirmed |
| `onBehalfOf` is populated on a live path (OAuth agent principals, `/mcp`) | `runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts:191` | confirmed |
| middleware mutates the operation context in place | `security-plugin.ts:1159` (`sc.__readScope = …`) | confirmed |
| stale-scope leak `resolveWriteScopeForSharing` prevents | `security-plugin.ts:2516` | confirmed |

**One correction to the card**, worth recording because it narrows the blast
radius: the projection reaches **`canEdit` only**, not `buildReadFilter` /
`canDelete`. This module takes the sharing service as
`Pick<ISharingService, 'canEdit'>` and calls it from exactly one site
(`canEditParent`, the update/delete gate). Reads are gated by a separate
middleware that re-enters the engine.

## Shape chosen, and why

The card named two candidates. **Chosen: forward the envelope minus the
middleware-private keys.**

The projection was doing **two jobs**, and only one of them was correct:

- **Stripping the middleware-private keys — correct, and preserved.** The keys
  carry the access DEPTH resolved for `sys_comment`, the object of the operation,
  while these gates ask about the **parent record's** object. They are now
  dropped by the **`__` prefix** instead of by name: the same channel carries the
  engine's other operation-private markers — `__expandRead` *waives the
  object-level CRUD check* (`security-plugin.ts:1082`), `__referentialFieldClear`
  the referential-clear write — so a four-name deny list would have been both
  incomplete today and stale the day a fifth key is stamped.
- **Stripping the principal fields — the defect.** Restored in full.

**Why not the second candidate (resolve the parent object's own depth).** The
only tool a package outside `plugin-security` has for it is the published
`ISecurityService.resolveWriteScope`, and `getEffectiveScope` returns **`'org'`
when no permission set matches the object** (`permission-evaluator.ts:255`) — the
fail-open the service's own doc block flags as "non-authoritative on its own".
Handing that to `canEdit` as `__writeScope` would make `matchesOwnerScope`
return `true` for **any owned row** of an unmatched object. Requiring it would
also give `plugin-audit` a new cross-plugin service seam it deliberately does
not have.

**Do the two shapes diverge in enforcement outcome?** On the question this card
is about — the fail-closed contract — **no**: `resolveWriteScope` itself returns
`'own'` for an `onBehalfOf` context, so the delegated principal is refused
identically under either shape, and `hasWriteBypass` fails closed under both.
They diverge only on an **orthogonal widening** question: whether this gate
should run the parent's owner-match at the caller's real write DEPTH (candidate
2, permissive) or at the narrowest `own` (candidate 1 — and, byte-for-byte, what
the projection already did). This PR does not take that decision in either
direction; it is filed separately so it can be decided on its own evidence.

## Severity measurement (asked for by triage — reported as measured)

**Can the agent's scope-derived ceiling carry `modifyAllRecords`? No.**
`scopesToAgentPermissionSets` (`spec/src/ai/mcp.zod.ts:187`) can return exactly
three set names, and all three are literal declarations in
`plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts`:
`mcp_agent_data_read` (`{'*': {allowRead}}`), `mcp_agent_data_write`
(`{'*': {allowRead, allowCreate, allowEdit, allowDelete}}` + managed-object write
denies), `mcp_agent_restricted` (`{}`). None carries `viewAllRecords` /
`modifyAllRecords`. In the built-in set catalogue only `admin_full_access` and
`organization_admin` carry the bit. So on the live `/mcp` producer path the
stripped guard is **latent, not exploitable today** —
`hasSuperuserWriteBypass` would return `false` anyway.

**But the projection dropped a second field that is load-bearing on the same
path, and this one is not latent.** `resolvePermissionSetsForContext`
(`security-plugin.ts:3024-3034`) keys the ADR-0090 D10 rule — an agent's grants
are *exactly* its ceiling, the additive human baseline must NOT apply, "or its
write bit would silently widen a read-only agent past the scope the user
consented to" — on `context?.principalKind === 'agent'`. `principalKind` was
stripped by the same projection, so an agent reaching `hasWriteBypass` through
this gate was resolved **as a human** and had the deployment's
`fallbackPermissionSet` appended to its ceiling. With the built-in default
(`member_default`) that superset still cannot mint `modifyAllRecords`, so it is
not an exploit with stock defaults either — but the baseline is
deployment-configurable (ADR-0056 D7: an app's `isDefault` profile), and the
widening itself is unconditional.

**Honest bound:** a documented fail-closed invariant was not honoured, and the
agent ceiling was not honoured, on a live path; neither is exploitable into a
`modifyAllRecords` bypass with the built-in permission sets. Nothing here
establishes a release-blocking exploit, so the `target:v17` re-grade triage
offered is **not** claimed.

## Tests (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit`, +6)

Shape pins, then outcome pins — the latter drive the gate through a **double**
that models the two contract clauses it depends on (`SharingService.checkEdit`'s
positive bases and `ISecurityService.hasWriteBypass`'s three guard lines).
`plugin-audit` does not depend on `plugin-security`, so modelling the contract is
the only way to pin the outcome on this side of the seam; the double's ordering
mirrors production (`matchesOwnerScope` reads the depth key before ownership).

1. forwards the whole envelope **minus** the operation-private keys
2. hands the service a **copy**, so a callee stamping `__writeScope` cannot write
   back into the operation context
3. **refuses** a delegated principal whose sets carry `modifyAllRecords`
4. keeps an **agent** principal capped at its ceiling (no additive baseline)
5. does **not** carry `sys_comment`'s depth into the parent's owner-match
6. read side: the parent probe is handed the envelope minus the private keys

## Reverse verification — predicted before running, measured after

| Mutation | Predicted RED | Measured RED | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| **M1** body back to the 5-field projection | 1, 3, 4 | 1, 3, 4 (41 pass) | none |
| **M2** `return exec;` (the naive fix) | 1, 2, 5 | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (39 pass) | **3 and 4 also went red — unpredicted** |
| **M3** read-path strip reverted only | 6 | 6 (43 pass) | none |

**The M2 delta, explained rather than filed away.** I predicted the delegation
tests would stay green under `return exec;` because `onBehalfOf` is forwarded
there too. They went red because the stale `__writeScope: 'org'` short-circuits
`matchesOwnerScope` **before** the bypass probe is ever consulted — so the naive
fix does not merely add a stale key beside a restored guard, it makes the stale
depth **dominate** the very guard this card exists to restore. I re-read the
double against `sharing-service.ts` before believing it: the ordering is
faithful, and the fixture's parent row has a non-null owner, which is the
precondition production's fast-exit sits behind.

**Guards that correctly stayed green, stated rather than hidden:** tests 2 and 5
under M1 — the old projection also returned a fresh object and also stripped the
depth key, so a guard for those two properties *should* pass under that mutation.
They are there to stop the fix from regressing in the other direction, which is
exactly what M2 measured.

## Gates (local, this package)

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit test` | **9 files / 143 tests passed** |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit typecheck` | **clean** (`tsc --noEmit`) |
| `eslint packages/plugins/plugin-audit --no-inline-config` | **0 errors, 0 warnings** |
| `pnpm check:org-identifier` | **OK** (1726 files, no `organizationId` spelling added) |

## Deliberately not done

- **No parent-object depth resolution** (candidate 2) — a widening; filed as
  **#7144** for the maintainer, with the fail-open that blocks the obvious
  implementation written up there.
- **`SharingExecutionContext` left exported** — its removal belongs to #7135.
- **The identical projection in `service-storage`'s attachment kit**
  (`attachment-access-hooks.ts:70`) — same five fields, same `canEdit` consumer,
  different package. Filed as **#7145** rather than fixed (Prime Directive #10).
- No `content/docs/releases/` edit; the changeset is this PR's input.
